school.tagged_body:
How Does AI Learn?

{{v:Artificial intelligence}}, or AI, is everywhere today. It {{v:recommends}} videos and {{v:translates}} languages. It even {{g:helps doctors find|help + 목적어 + 동사원형: (목적어)가 ~하도록 돕다}} {{v:diseases}}. But how does AI learn?

{{t:AI learns a little like children}}. Let's say you {{g:want to teach|to부정사 명사적 용법(목적어): ~하기를 원하다}} a computer about cats. First, you show the computer {{v:thousands of}} pictures. Each picture has a {{v:label}}: "cat" or "not cat." The computer studies these {{v:examples}}. Slowly, it finds {{v:patterns}}, like {{v:pointed}} ears and {{v:whiskers}}. {{g:When it makes a mistake|시간 접속사 when + 주어 + 동사: ~할 때}}, it changes its {{v:guess}} and tries again. {{g:The more examples it sees, the better it becomes|the 비교급 + 주어 + 동사, the 비교급 + 주어 + 동사: ~할수록 더 …하다}}.

But AI is not {{v:perfect}}. It only learns from {{v:data}}, and people give it this data. {{g:If the data has mistakes|조건의 if: if절은 미래의 일이라도 현재시제(has)를 쓴다}}, the AI will learn those mistakes, too. For example, let's say an AI sees pictures of white cats {{v:most of the time}}. Then it {{g:may not|may not + 동사원형: ~하지 못할지도 모른다}} {{v:recognize}} black cats well. For the same reason, AI can sometimes make {{v:unfair}} {{v:decisions}} about people.

So we {{g:should always check|should + 동사원형: ~해야 한다 (빈도부사 always는 조동사 뒤)}} AI's answers again. {{t:AI is a powerful tool}}, but it cannot {{v:take the place of}} human thinking and {{v:judgment}}.

{{v:Artificial intelligence}}, or AI, {{g:has become|현재완료(결과): ~이 되었다 (지금도 그렇다)}} part of our everyday lives. It recommends {{g:videos we might enjoy|목적격 관계대명사 생략: videos (that) we might enjoy}}, translates between languages in seconds, and even {{v:assists}} doctors in {{v:detecting}} diseases. But have you ever wondered how AI actually learns?

In some ways, {{t:AI learns much like children do}}. {{g:Suppose you wanted|Suppose + 가정법 과거: ~한다고 가정해 보자 (과거형으로 현재 상황을 가정)}} to teach a computer to {{v:recognize}} cats. First, the computer {{g:would be shown|조동사 + 수동태: would be + p.p.}} thousands of images, {{g:each labeled|독립분사구문: each (being) labeled — 각각 ~라고 표시된 채로}} either "cat" or "not cat." By {{v:analyzing}} these examples, the computer {{v:gradually}} {{v:identifies}} common patterns, such as pointed ears and whiskers. {{g:Whenever|복합관계부사 whenever: ~할 때마다}} it makes an error, it {{v:adjusts}} its guess and tries again. {{g:The more examples it is exposed to, the more accurate it becomes|the 비교급 ~, the 비교급 …: ~할수록 더 …하다 / be exposed to: ~에 노출되다}}.

However, AI is {{v:far from}} perfect. It can learn only from the data {{g:that humans provide|목적격 관계대명사 that: 앞의 the data를 꾸민다}}. If that data {{v:contains}} errors, the AI will {{v:inevitably}} {{v:absorb}} those errors as well. For instance, if an AI {{g:is trained|수동태: be + p.p. (훈련되다)}} mainly on images of white cats, it may {{v:struggle}} to recognize black cats. For the same reason, AI can sometimes make {{v:biased}} or unfair decisions about people.

{{g:This is why|This is why + 주어 + 동사: 이것이 ~하는 이유이다 (그래서 ~하다)}} we should always double-check the information AI gives us. {{t:AI is undoubtedly a powerful tool, but it can never replace human thinking and judgment}}.

prestudy.tagged_body:
How Does AI Learn?

Artificial intelligence, or AI, {{g:has become|현재완료(결과): ~이 되었다}} deeply {{v:embedded}} in {{v:contemporary}} life. It {{v:curates}} video recommendations, translates languages almost {{v:instantaneously}}, and even assists {{v:physicians}} in {{v:diagnosing}} diseases. Yet have you ever stopped {{g:to consider|stop + to부정사: ~하기 위해 멈추다 (stop + -ing: ~하던 것을 멈추다와 구별)}} how AI actually {{v:acquires}} its abilities?

Remarkably, {{g:the way AI learns|the way + 주어 + 동사: ~하는 방식 (the way와 how는 함께 쓰지 않는다)}} somewhat {{v:resembles}} the way children learn. {{g:Imagine attempting to train|imagine + 동명사 / attempt + to부정사}} a computer to {{v:identify}} cats. {{v:Initially}}, the computer {{g:is presented with|수동태: be presented with ~을 제시받다}} thousands of images, {{g:each of which has been labeled|계속적 용법 관계대명사(each of which) + 현재완료 수동태(has been p.p.)}} either "cat" or "not cat." By {{v:examining}} these examples, the computer {{v:progressively}} {{v:detects}} {{v:recurring}} patterns, such as pointed ears and whiskers. Whenever it makes an {{v:incorrect}} {{v:prediction}}, it {{v:modifies}} its guess and attempts once more. {{g:The more examples it encounters, the more accurate its predictions become|the 비교급 ~, the 비교급 …: ~할수록 더 …하다}}.

Nevertheless, AI is {{v:by no means}} {{v:infallible}}. It {{g:is capable of learning|be capable of + 동명사: ~할 수 있다}} only from the data that humans {{v:supply}}. {{g:Should that data contain flaws|if 생략 도치: Should + 주어 + 동사원형 = If that data should contain flaws (혹시 ~라면)}}, the AI will inevitably {{v:reproduce}} those {{v:flaws}}. For instance, {{g:an AI trained predominantly on images of white cats|과거분사구 후치 수식: trained ~ 가 an AI를 꾸민다}} may fail to recognize black cats {{v:reliably}}. For precisely the same reason, AI systems can {{v:occasionally}} make biased or {{v:discriminatory}} decisions about people.

{{v:Consequently}}, {{t:we should always verify the information that AI provides}}. {{g:Although|양보 접속사 although: 비록 ~이지만}} AI is an {{v:extraordinarily}} powerful tool, {{t:it can never substitute for human reasoning and judgment}}.

questions.q: Which of the following best summarizes the writer's central argument?

questions.answer: Because AI learns only from human-supplied data, it can reproduce that data's flaws, so its output must be verified by human judgment.

essays.q: Summarize the passage in three English sentences: (1) how AI learns, (2) why its results can be flawed, and (3) what the writer recommends.
essays.sampleAnswer: AI learns in a way that resembles children, by examining many labeled examples, detecting recurring patterns, and modifying its guesses after incorrect predictions. Because it can learn only from the data humans supply, it reproduces any flaws in that data, which can even lead to discriminatory decisions about people. Consequently, the writer recommends that we always verify what AI provides, since it can never substitute for human reasoning and judgment.
